Give feedback

For 2 adults and 4 days, I’d avoid trying to “do all of Goa.” You’ll spend too much time travelling. A good modest-budget trip is North Goa as the base + one South Goa day. North Goa gives you beaches, cafés and nightlife, while South Goa gives you the quieter couple-friendly beach experience. 
PunyaPaths
+1

A practical 4-day plan
Day	Plan	Approx. spend for 2
Day 1	Arrive → check-in → Anjuna/Vagator → sunset	₹1,500–2,500
Day 2	Chapora Fort → Vagator → Anjuna → Baga/Calangute evening	₹2,000–3,000
Day 3	South Goa: Palolem + Agonda → sunset → return	₹2,500–3,500
Day 4	Candolim/Aguada → Panjim/Fontainhas → depart	₹1,500–2,500
Where I'd stay

For a modest budget, I'd pick Anjuna/Vagator/Arpora rather than Baga itself. You get decent accommodation, restaurants and nightlife without paying the Baga premium.

Some currently listed budget options include:

goSTOPS PLUS Goa Vagator — good if you're okay with a hostel-style property.

Moustache Goa Luxuria — a more comfortable budget option around Vagator.

Falcon Resorts Goa by Dia Hotels — inexpensive hotel option around Calangute.

Current travel guides put basic rooms/guesthouses around ₹600–₹1,500+ per night, depending heavily on season and location. 
News9live

Transport

Rent one scooter if both adults are comfortable riding. That's usually the best way to keep a 4-day Goa trip inexpensive; current guides quote roughly ₹300–₹400/day for basic scooters, although actual rates vary by season. 
News9live

For example, Bike Rentals in Goa is around Candolim, while Vaggis bike and car rental is around Arpora.

If neither of you wants to ride, I'd skip the scooter and use taxis selectively rather than renting a car for four days.

Food strategy

This is where you can save a surprising amount.

Breakfast: ₹150–250/person

Local lunch/thali: ₹150–300/person

One nicer dinner: ₹600–1,000 for two

Keep beach cafés/shacks to one meal a day

Don't make every meal a “Goa Instagram café”

You can comfortably eat for roughly ₹1,000–1,500/day for two without eating badly.

Rough total budget

For 4 days / 3 nights, two adults, excluding your travel to/from Goa:

Stay: ₹4,000–7,000

Scooter + fuel: ₹1,500–2,500

Food: ₹4,000–6,000

Activities/entries: ₹1,000–2,000

Local transport/misc: ₹1,000–2,000

Total: roughly ₹12,000–19,500 for two, excluding flights/trains/buses.

If you're travelling from Bangalore, I'd strongly consider an overnight train/bus or a cheap flight depending on your dates. Recent 2026 travel estimates put Bangalore–Goa trips at quite a range depending on transport and booking time. 
Tripz Search

My sweet spot: budget ₹18–25k for two including transport from Bangalore, and spend the money on a nicer room + one good dinner rather than expensive activities.

If you tell me your exact dates + whether you're travelling from Bangalore, I can make this into a day-by-day plan with specific hotels, transport and a realistic total budget.

What matters financially

For 50 employees, the biggest hidden costs are usually change/cancellation fees, payment fees, service fees and employee time, rather than subscription pricing.

Trip.Biz is worth getting a quote from if you have significant international travel. myBiz makes the fee structure particularly transparent, but its 1.5% payment charge can become meaningful at scale. Yatra has useful free-rescheduling benefits, while EMTDesk emphasises managed support and expense controls.

Before signing, ask each provider for a sample ₹10 lakh annual travel-spend invoice showing every fee, GST treatment, cancellation deduction and refund timeline.
